inference_path.alpha_storage: for a stored prototype word alpha is one-hot; for an unseen S it is computed
inference_path.molecule_F: mean over the fixed views; fallback head for molecules without a cut
inference_path.molecule_to_views: bridge cuts + fixed <=4 view selection (structure processing)
inference_path.stored_C: b(C), k(C) from a Train-environment table if cached
inference_path.stored_S: a_words(S), q_words(S) from the 136-word table (one-hot alpha)
inference_path.unseen_S: encoder z_S -> a(S), q(S) -> response on the 16-env Train panel -> simplex projection to alpha over the stored prototypes; no GNN re-run per environment

storage_note: The 136 stored words 702 -> 136 do not remove the encoder. The encoder (and the a/q heads) is still required for a new S to compute alpha; k(C)/b(C) are still required for the C side. The tables above are materialised only if an application chooses to cache them; the model weights remain 198k parameters.
view_stats_note: `stored_S` means the S fragment is one of the 136 stored words; `stored_C` means the C fragment is one of the 9191 Train environment fragments. A pure lookup view needs both. The unseen-S fraction is not a generalisation claim: these fragments exist in Val/Test but were not Train words.
